amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Flood Control and Land Development of City Camp Lagoon, 16.410157N, 120.586109E, Baguio City
amendments.justification:
The proposed project is necessary to address recurring flooding, inadequate drainage capacity, and water management concerns within and around the City Camp Lagoon area. During periods of heavy rainfall, insufficient drainage and flood control facilities can result in water accumulation, damage to properties and public infrastructure, disruption of transportation and community activities, and risks to public health and safety.
The project will provide comprehensive flood mitigation through the construction and improvement of drainage and flood control structures, together with appropriate land development works. These interventions will improve the conveyance and management of stormwater, reduce flood risks, protect lives and properties, and enhance the safety and functionality of the area. Implementing a coordinated and long-term flood control solution will help reduce potential future losses, strengthen climate and disaster resilience, and support the orderly and sustainable development of the City Camp Lagoon area and strongly recommended by the Local Government of Baguio City.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction/ Upgrading/ Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads - Secondary Roads - G. Araneta Avenue (S05617LZ) - K0009 + 346 - K0009 + 684, Quezon City
amendments.justification:
This is necessary to address the recurring flooding affecting G. Araneta Avenue and its surrounding areas by improving the stormwater conveyance capacity along the identified road section. The project involves the installation of High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) pipes to provide an efficient drainage system for collecting and conveying stormwater toward the appropriate downstream facility.

The proposed drainage improvement will form an integral part of the existing drainage network along G. Araneta Avenue. The installation of HDPE pipes will improve drainage capacity and continuity, allowing stormwater runoff from the roadway and adjacent areas to be more effectively conveyed and reducing water accumulation during moderate to heavy rainfall.

The proposed multi-barrel HDPE pipe system is intended to increase the available flow capacity toward the outfall and address the possible bottleneck in the existing drainage network that may be contributing to the persistence of flooding in the surrounding area.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction/ Upgrading/ Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads - Tertiary Roads - Mother Ignacia Ave. (S05365LZ) - K0010 +203 - K0010 + 436, Quezon City
amendments.justification: This is necessary to address the flooding problem affecting the area by providing an improved and continuous drainage facility capable of conveying stormwater along the affected road section. The project will provide a reinforced concrete box culvert integrated within the roadway to improve the collection and conveyance of surface runoff and provide a more reliable drainage pathway for the surrounding area. It will serve as the upstream drainage facility that will connect to the proposed box culvert along Sgt. Esguerra Avenue, which will in turn provide the necessary connection toward the existing box culvert system along Panay Avenue. amendments.projectTitle: Construction/ Upgrading/ Rehabilitation of Drainage along National Roads - Tertiary Roads, Mother Ignacia Ave. (S05365LZ) - K0009 + 223 - K0009 +523, Quezon City
amendments.justification:
This is necessary to address the persistent and severe flooding occurring along the section between Timog Avenue and Scout Borromeo Street, Quezon City. During heavy rainfall, floodwaters in the area reach significant depths, resulting in the submergence of parked vehicles and causing disruption to road users, nearby establishments, properties, and surrounding infrastructure. The recurring nature and severity of the flooding indicate the need for a permanent and adequately designed drainage improvement rather than continued reliance on existing drainage facilities.

The proposed project will provide an improved drainage system along the affected section of Mother Ignacia Avenue to enhance the collection and conveyance of stormwater. The proposed drainage facilities, including large-capacity pipe drainage, manholes, and water interceptors, are designed to provide a more efficient pathway for stormwater runoff and improve the overall drainage performance of the roadway. The project alignment extends from the vicinity of Timog Avenue toward Scout Borromeo Street, directly covering the identified flood-prone section.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Interceptor along Toctocan Road, Brgys. Manresa (Sta. 0+004.00P - Sta. 0+130.00P), Masambong (Sta. 0+005.30 - Sta. 0+016.00, Sta. 0+210.00 - Sta. 261.60, Sta. 0+410.00 - Sta. 0+484.10A, Sta. 0+450.00 - Sta. 0+460.00B), and Apolonio Samson (Sta. 0+460.00B-Sta.0+484.10B), Quezon City
amendments.justification:
This is necessary to improve the existing drainage system and address the collection and conveyance of stormwater along the identified sections of Toctocan Road. The project covers critical sections within the affected barangays, where inadequate drainage capacity may result in the accumulation of surface water and localized flooding during periods of heavy rainfall. The construction of an interceptor will provide an additional drainage facility to efficiently collect and convey runoff, thereby improving the overall performance of the existing drainage network.

The proposed interceptor will enhance the capacity of the drainage system by intercepting surface runoff before it accumulates along the roadway and adjacent areas. The facility will facilitate the proper conveyance of stormwater toward the appropriate drainage outfall, reducing water accumulation along the road and minimizing the potential for flooding. The project will also help preserve the condition and serviceability of the roadway by reducing prolonged exposure to standing water and improving the overall drainage of the affected sections.

Furthermore, the construction of the interceptor will contribute to the improvement of flood mitigation measures within the surrounding communities of Barangays Manresa, Masambong, and Apolonio Samson. By improving the collection and conveyance of stormwater, the project will help reduce the occurrence and duration of localized flooding, improve road accessibility during rainfall events, and protect nearby properties and public infrastructure. The project will likewise support the efficient functioning of the existing drainage network and enhance the resilience of the affected communities against heavy rainfall and flooding.

amendments.projectTitle: Improvement of Road Dike leading to Navotas Pumping Station No. 1 (C0+000 - C0+385) along Navotas Coastal Dike, Navotas City
amendments.justification:
The Road Dike leading to Navotas Pumping Station No. 1 along Navotas Coastal Dike, Navotas City requires improvement to enhance its structural condition, accessibility, and overall functionality as part of the flood protection and drainage infrastructure serving the surrounding communities. The existing road dike serves as an important access route to the pumping station and forms part of the coastal flood protection system. Improvement of the facility is necessary to ensure its reliability and continued functionality, particularly during periods of heavy rainfall, high tide, and other conditions that may affect the operation and maintenance of the pumping station.

The proposed improvement will enhance the condition and serviceability of the road dike, providing safer and more reliable access to Navotas Pumping Station No. 1 for operation, maintenance, inspection, and emergency response activities. The improvement will also help protect the integrity of the dike and its associated facilities against deterioration and other factors that may compromise its effectiveness as part of the flood mitigation system. Ensuring adequate access to the pumping station is essential for the timely deployment of personnel, equipment, and materials, particularly during critical flooding events.

Furthermore, the improvement of the road dike will contribute to the overall effectiveness of the flood management system in Navotas City by supporting the continuous operation and maintenance of the pumping station. A reliable access route will facilitate immediate response to equipment failures, drainage concerns, and other operational requirements, thereby helping minimize flood risks, protect nearby communities and properties, and strengthen the resilience of the surrounding area against flooding and other climate-related hazards.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Dupinga Sabo Dam, Gabaldon, Nueva Ecija
amendments.justification:
The proposed project is necessary due to the continuing sedimentation and erosion risks affecting the Dupinga River and the downstream Coronel-Santur River system. The Master Plan identifies Dupinga River as one of the priority tributaries originating from the Sierra Madre where a Sabo Dam is proposed to address the continuous supply of unstable sediments from landslides and highly erodible upstream riverbanks.

To address this condition and preserve the hydraulic capacity of the downstream river system, the proposed Sabo Dam will intercept and retain unstable sediment and debris transported from the upstream watershed, thereby reducing the sediment load reaching the Coronel-Santur River. This intervention will help minimize progressive riverbed aggradation and sediment deposition, which can reduce the conveyance capacity of downstream channels and compromise the effectiveness of existing and planned flood-control infrastructure. The Master Plan recognizes Sabo Dams as structural countermeasures for river-system erosion and sediment management, complementing downstream flood-control measures.

Considering the continuing sediment supply from the upstream Sierra Madre watershed and the strategic role of Dupinga River in the Coronel-Santur River system, the proposed Dupinga River Sabo Dam is strongly recommended

Considering the continuing sediment supply from the upstream Sierra Madre watershed and the strategic role of Anipa River as a tributary of the Coronel-Santur River system, the proposed Anipa River Sabo Dam is strongly recommended for funding under the FY 2027 infrastructure program. Its implementation will advance the priority measures identified in the Pampanga River Basin Master Plan and help protect the long-term capacity and performance of downstream flood-control infrastructure.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Flood Mitigation Structure along Pampanga River and Bagbag River, Brgy. Frances - Gatbuca - Bulusan - Sta.Lucia, Calumpit Bulacan (Sta. 0+000 - Sta. 1+900, Sta. 0+000 - Sta. 1+738)
amendments.justification: Barangays Frances, Gatbuca, Bulusan, and Sta. Lucia sit within the natural floodplain of the Pampanga and Bagbag River system, where the existing riverbanks have limited freeboard and channel capacity relative to peak flood discharge. During heavy or prolonged rainfall, particularly during typhoons and the southwest monsoon, river flow can exceed what the natural banks can hold, causing water to spill over into nearby homes, farmlands, and roads. Because the banks were never engineered to handle this volume of flow, even moderate storms can trigger flooding in these areas.The proposed structure will effectively raise the flood-carrying capacity of the river at these critical points by reinforcing and elevating the containment along the banks. This means a higher volume of floodwater can pass through or be held within the river system before it overflows, directly reducing how often and how badly these communities get flooded. In short, the project fixes the actual weak point, the undersized channel capacity, rather than just dealing with the floodwater after it has already spread into the community.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Flood Mitigation Structure along Halang River, Hagonoy, Bulacan (Sta. 0+000 - Sta. 2+708, Sta. 0+000 - Sta. 2+418)
amendments.justification:
Hagonoy is a low-lying coastal municipality where the Halang and Hagonoy River system discharges into Manila Bay, making it subject to a compound flooding problem driven by two simultaneous forces. First, during high tide, seawater from Manila Bay pushes back into the river mouth and inland waterways, reducing the hydraulic gradient available for the river to drain and effectively narrowing its usable conveyance capacity at that moment. Second, during heavy rainfall events, the river system also receives backflooding from the Pampanga River, adding volume that the channel must accommodate on top of local runoff. When these two conditions occur together, typically during typhoons or intense monsoon rainfall coinciding with high tide, the combined water level in the river exceeds what the existing channel and banks can carry, causing water to spill into adjacent residential and agricultural areas for extended periods.

The proposed flood mitigation structure will increase the effective conveyance capacity of the river at the affected reaches, allowing the channel to accommodate a higher combined volume from tidal backwater and river backflow before overtopping occurs. By raising this threshold, the structure reduces the frequency and depth of inundation even when both flood drivers occur simultaneously, and shortens the time it takes for the river to eventually clear the excess water once tide levels recede. This gives Hagonoy a meaningfully higher level of flood protection against the specific compound tidal-fluvial condition that drives its recurring flooding.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Retarding Basin at South Central School Open Grounds, Brgy. Santo Cristo, Baliwag, Bulacan (14.95626, 120.8967)
amendments.justification: The project is a crucial flood-mitigation intervention engineered to address severe localized stormwater runoff and inundation risks in the surrounding area. Utilizing the available open grounds at Baliwag South Central School provides a strategic, dual-purpose spatial footprint to capture, temporarily store, and attenuate peak flood volumes during intense rainfall events and typhoons. Hydrologically, the retarding basin acts as a discharge-control mechanism, preventing surrounding municipal drainage systems from becoming surcharged and gradually releasing stored water at a safe, controlled rate.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Retarding Basin at Brgy. Bulihan, Malolos City, Bulacan (14.859608, 120.810933)
amendments.justification: The implementation of this project is a vital civil engineering intervention designed to address severe, recurring localized flooding along major urban arterial corridors and residential areas in Malolos City. Barangay Bulihan serves as a critical commercial, institutional, and transport hub—notably traversed by the MacArthur Highway and hosting major educational institutions such as Bulacan State University—making it highly susceptible to significant surface runoff accumulation during heavy monsoon rains and typhoon events. Due to dense urban development, high ground impermeability, and low-elevation topography, existing drainage conduits rapidly become surcharged, leading to prolonged waterlogging that disrupts traffic, damages property, and poses severe safety risks to thousands of commuters, students, and residents daily.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Retarding Basin along Sampaguita Road, Brgy. Santo Rosario, City of Malolos, Bulacan (14.839380, 120.814731)
amendments.justification: The construction of a retarding basin along Sampaguita Road, Barangay Santa Rosario, City of Malolos, Bulacan, is an essential infrastructure project designed to mitigate severe localized flooding, severe runoff accumulation, and drainage bottlenecks along a major arterial corridor. Sampaguita Road serves as a critical local access route, but its low elevation and dense surrounding development leave it highly vulnerable to rapid stormwater accumulation during intense rainfall and typhoons. Installing an engineered retarding basin along this roadway provides indispensable temporary detention capacity, intercepting heavy surface runoff before it can submerge the road network and surrounding residential structures. By systematically controlling the discharge rate of impounded floodwaters into the main municipal drainage outlets, the facility effectively lowers peak flood levels and shortens inundation times.

amendments.projectTitle: Rehabilitation of Road with Slope Protection along Sto. Tomas - Minalin Tail Dike (Minalin Section), including Revetment Works, Sta. 9+860 - Sta. 10+340, Brgy. Sta. Catalina, Minalin, Pampanga

Construction of Nature Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Masukol, Paombong, Bulacan (14.762244, 120.770711)
amendments.justification: The implementation of the Construction of Nature-Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Masukol, Paombong, Bulacan is technically essential to mitigate severe coastal erosion, storm surges, and tidal flooding that threaten vulnerable coastal communities along Manila Bay. Traditional grey infrastructure often suffers from long-term degradation and high maintenance costs in dynamic marine environments, whereas a nature-based coastal defense—such as mangrove restoration, living breakwaters, or bio-engineered revetments—provides adaptive, self-sustaining shore stabilization. By trapping sediments, dissipating wave energy, and enhancing natural ecosystems, this sustainable intervention delivers long-term disaster risk reduction, restores aquatic biodiversity, and protects vital local livelihoods and infrastructure against accelerating climate change impacts.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Nature Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Sta. Cruz, Paombong, Bulacan (14.758897, 120.792747)
amendments.justification: The implementation of the Construction of Nature-Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Sta. Cruz, Paombong, Bulacan is technically essential to mitigate severe coastal erosion, tidal inundation, and storm surge vulnerabilities along the low-lying Manila Bay coastline. Traditional concrete seawalls are prone to structural undermining and high lifecycle maintenance costs in dynamic wetland conditions, whereas a nature-based coastal defense—incorporating elements like mangrove greenbelts, sediment-trapping permeable brushwood dams, or living breakwaters—offers an adaptive, self-reinforcing buffer. By attenuating wave energy, capturing natural sediment to combat land subsidence, and reinforcing shoreline integrity, this sustainable engineering approach provides long-term flood resilience, safeguards local coastal communities, and enhances estuarine ecosystems without disrupting natural hydrologic functions.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Nature Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Tibaguin, Hagonoy, Bulacan (14.772167, 120.752300)
amendments.justification: The implementation of the Construction of Nature-Based Solution Coastal Defense in Barangay Tibaguin, Hagonoy, Bulacan is technically essential to mitigate severe coastal erosion, high-tide inundation, and extreme storm surge risks along the vulnerable shoreline of Manila Bay. Traditional concrete seawalls often face structural failures, scouring, and exorbitant maintenance costs due to rapid land subsidence and shifting coastal dynamics in Hagonoy. By contrast, a nature-based coastal defense—such as integrated mangrove vegetation belts, mudflat restoration, or permeable wave-attenuating structures—provides an adaptive, self-sustaining barrier. This eco-engineering solution absorbs wave energy, promotes natural sediment deposition to raise ground elevation, and strengthens shoreline resilience while preserving local estuarine ecosystems and safeguarding the lives, homes, and aquaculture livelihoods of Barangay Tibaguin.

amendments.projectTitle:
Construction of Retarding Basin at Engr. Virgilio V. Dionisio Memorial Highschool, Brgy. Poblacion, Pulilan, Bulacan 
(14.8999, 120.8472)
amendments.justification: The construction of a retarding basin at Engr. Virgilio V. Dionisio Memorial High School in Brgy. Poblacion, Pulilan, Bulacan is a critical civil engineering intervention designed to attenuate excessive stormwater runoff and mitigate acute localized flooding within school grounds and surrounding low-lying communities. By temporarily impounding peak runoff volumes during intense precipitation events and releasing them at a controlled rate into the municipal drainage network, the basin relieves hydraulic pressure on existing conveyance structures, prevents surface inundation, and reduces soil erosion. Implementing this infrastructure safeguards vital academic facilities and administrative assets, minimizes flood-related disruptions to instructional operations, and guarantees a secure, resilient learning environment for students and personnel during heavy rains.

amendments.projectTitle: Construction of Retarding Basin at Government Center, Barangay Peñabatan, Pulilan, Bulacan (14.9274, 120.8415)
amendments.justification: The construction of a retarding basin at the Government Center in Barangay Peñabatan, Pulilan, Bulacan is technically necessary to mitigate acute localized flooding and manage peak stormwater runoff generated during extreme rainfall events. By providing temporary off-stream or in-line volume storage, the basin will effectively lower peak discharge rates into the surrounding drainage network, alleviating hydraulic pressure on downstream channels and preventing inundation of critical municipal administrative infrastructure. Furthermore, controlled attenuation and gradual release of floodwaters protect surrounding public facilities and residential zones from soil erosion, structural water damage, and severe operational disruptions, thereby ensuring climate resilience and continuous delivery of essential civic services. During dry season, water impounded will be served as irrigation water in farmland.

amendments.projectTitle: Repair/Maintenance of Porac River Revetment 5, Sta. 0+000 - Sta. 0+240, Sto. Cristo, Lubao, Pampanga
amendments.justification:
The proposed project has been identified as necessary, urgent, and vital to address the extensive structural collapse of the existing river dike revetment caused by the recent typhoons Luis, Maymay, Neneng and Pilandok, and the enhanced Southwest Moonsoon (Habagat). 

The structural integrity of the riverbank embankment is severely compromised and at risk of total failure without immediate intervention. The river corridor serves as a critical natural drainage channel subjected to intense seasonal runoff and high-velocity flood flows during heavy rainfall events. 

The current riverbank collapse and localized erosion directly expose adjacent residential structures, public utilities, and nearby agricultural land to imminent flooding, land loss, and structural destruction. Reconstructing the damaged slope protection is essential to provide the high erosion resistance, hydraulic stability, and long-term durability required to withstand scouring, thereby protecting community lives and properties.
